title: Lesson 5: BLESS - Share Your Story and the Gospel
description: Sharing the gospel is telling the story of Jesus and how He has changed your story. After praying, listening, eating, and serving, the bridge of relationship is built. This lesson gives you three stories to hold in every faith conversation, theirs, yours, and His, and a simple picture you can draw on a napkin to share the gospel anywhere.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to serve the way Jesus served, with a towel and a basin. Praying, listening, eating, and serving have all been building a bridge of relationship. This lesson is the moment you get to walk across it. Now you have something to say.

blocks.alt: A man who had been blind from birth, with his eyes open after being healed by Jesus

blocks.title: I Was Blind, Now I See
blocks.text:
Jesus once met a man who had been blind from birth. After Jesus healed him, the religious leaders dragged him in for an interrogation. They wanted theology. They wanted answers. They wanted him to take their side against Jesus.

The man did not have a sermon ready. He did not have a polished argument. He simply told them what he knew.

"One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see." (John 9:25)

That is sharing your faith at its simplest. You do not have to be a theologian. You do not need every answer. You just need to tell someone honestly what Jesus has done in your life, and then point them to the One who can do it in theirs.
That is the heart of this rhythm. You tell what Jesus has done for you, and you point to the One who can do it for them. The rest of this lesson helps you do it.
From Bridge to Crossing

When you have prayed for someone, listened to them, shared a meal, and shown up to serve, you have been given the opening to share. Sharing your faith in that kind of relationship feels natural, not awkward. The conversation has been on its way for a while. The Holy Spirit has been at work in you and in them long before this moment. The only thing left is for you to actually open your mouth.

How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching? And how are they to preach unless they are sent? As it is written, "How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the good news!"

Sharing the gospel is sharing the story of Jesus and how He has changed your story. You get to tell someone the story of Jesus' life, death, and resurrection, and how that story has rewritten the story of your own life. Ask yourself the question that sits under your Personal Ministry Map: "Does everyone who knows me know about the gospel?" If the answer is no, the people you have been BLESSing are exactly where to start.
Peter writes about the kind of readiness this calls for.
But in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect.

Notice the word Peter chose. Always be prepared, not always be presenting, because preparation is the internal work that gets done long before any conversation. You shape your story and learn the gospel so that when the moment comes, when a friend asks why you seem different or when a coworker opens up about a hard season, you are ready, not polished, not perfect, just ready.
5.1 - Of the people you have been blessing, whose conversation about Jesus feels ready?
Three Stories

Every faith conversation has three stories on the table: their story, your story, and His story. Hold them in that order. You listen first, you share your own story briefly, and then you point to Jesus.

blocks.title: Their Story, Your Story, His Story
content: Their story. Start by listening. Through the BLESS rhythms you already know something of what they carry, what they hope for, and where they hurt. Ask, ask again, and remember. When you have heard them, what you say next lands in their real life instead of bouncing off.
Your story. Tell what Jesus has done for you, in about a minute. Like the man born blind, you do not need every answer, only what you know.
His story. Point to Jesus: His life, His death for our sins, and His resurrection. This is the story that can change theirs, and it is the one you will learn to draw below.

blocks.text: Look again at the man in John 9. When the leaders questioned him, he told his story plainly. Later Jesus found him and showed him who He was, and the man said, "Lord, I believe" (John 9:38). Your story opens the door. His story is the one that saves.
Your Story: Keep It Short
Your story is a short bridge into His story, not the whole conversation. Keep it simple: "There was a time when ____, but then I met Jesus and discovered ____, and now I ____."
5.2 - Write one short testimony using that frame. Keep it plain enough to say in about one minute.
His Story: The 3 Circles

His story, the story of Jesus, is the heart of the gospel. There may come a moment in a conversation where what your friend needs is not just your story, but His. For that you need a tool. Something simple enough to draw on a napkin, clear enough that you do not stumble, and reproducible enough that the friend you share it with could turn around and share it with someone else.

The 3 Circles is a simple gospel picture many Christians use in ordinary conversations. Walk through it slowly below. Do not just read it, click through each step. By the end you will already be most of the way to being able to draw it from memory.
Walking Through the Diagram
God's Design. God created the world good and made you for a close relationship with Him. Life was meant to flow the way He designed it.

Sin and Brokenness. Instead of trusting God, people turned away and went their own way. The Bible calls that sin, and sin broke the world. Brokenness shows up in pain, sickness, and broken homes. The squiggly arrows are the ways people try to escape: money, success, relationships, distractions. They promise freedom, but they snap people back into the same brokenness.

The Gospel. God did not leave people stuck. He sent His Son Jesus down to earth, where Jesus lived without sin, died on the cross to pay for sin, and rose again on the third day. That is the good news in a sentence.

For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures.

Repent and Believe. The way back to God is not earning, it is turning. Repent means to turn from going your own way. Believe means to trust Jesus as Savior and King. Recover and Pursue. When you turn to Jesus, God forgives you, makes you new, and restores you to His design.
5.3 - Which part of the 3 Circles feels hardest to explain in your own words?
This Week's Practice

Most people never share the gospel because they do not feel ready. The way to feel ready is to practice with someone who already loves you. Drawing the 3 Circles for a Christian friend, your spouse, or a child takes the pressure off and helps the words come more naturally.

blocks.title: Practice Drawing the 3 Circles
content: Pick one person this week to walk through the 3 Circles with. A friend, a family member, or a trusted Christian works great as a first try.
Grab a napkin, a sheet of paper, or a whiteboard. Draw it as you talk, not before. Drawing as you go is what makes it feel natural.
Try all three stories: ask about their story, tell your one-minute story, then draw His.
End with a simple invitation: "Where do you see yourself on this picture? Where do you want to be? Is there anything keeping you from turning to Jesus today?"

blocks.text: 5.4 - Who will you draw the 3 Circles for this week?
Faithful, Not Successful

Here is a truth that takes the pressure off: faithful sharing is not measured by the response of the person you share with. It is measured by your willingness to offer the good news. You may be the first step in someone's story or the tenth. You may plant the seed and someone else may water it later.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.
Only God grows what is planted. Your job is to plant; His job is to grow. That frees you from the weight of having to convince anyone, and it frees the other person from feeling like a project.
Lesson 5 Review

Like the man born blind, you do not need a sermon ready. Sharing your faith is telling what Jesus has done for you and pointing to the One who can do it for them. Every faith conversation has three stories: theirs, yours, and His. You listen to theirs, you tell yours in about a minute, and you point to His with a simple picture like the 3 Circles. You do not need every answer or a perfect speech. Your job is to plant. God gives the growth, and He opens eyes the way He opened yours.
In the next lesson, you will carry the BLESS rhythms into your 2nd Space, the place where most of your week is spent.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?

The BLESS rhythms are adapted from BLESS: 5 Everyday Ways to Love Your Neighbor and Change the World by Dave Ferguson and Jon Ferguson. The 3 Circles is adapted from the 3 Circles Life Conversation Guide from the North American Mission Board.
